resources.lead: Reliable contacts and texts: at school, nationally and in law.
resources.efrei_intro: At school, several people can listen to you. Write to them by e-mail: you choose what you share.
resources.steps_title: How the disability office supports you

steps.title: First interview
steps.text: Building trust, respecting privacy, identifying needs, explaining the rules and the documents needed.

steps.title: Setting up accommodations
steps.text: The office uses internal tools to track accommodations.

steps.title: Talking with teaching teams
steps.text: If needed, depending on the disability: passing on instructions, practical situations, explanations.

steps.title: Follow-up throughout your studies
steps.text: The office checks that accommodations match your needs and attends exam boards if needed.

steps.title: Help entering the working world
steps.text: Partner companies are looking for graduates with disabilities.

resources.freq_title: The most common accommodations at school
resources.freq_intro: Separate rooms and extra time are the most common. Digital tools and specialised equipment play a growing role.
resources.types_text: Most supported situations are invisible disabilities: “dys” disorders (reading, writing, language) and disabling illnesses come first, followed by psychological, cognitive and motor difficulties, autism, and hearing or vision impairments. Each situation gets an individual response.
school: Several departments contribute to accessibility: information systems, transformation, student life, teaching innovation, cross-cutting projects and a research lab.
Many staff members have been trained in Mental Health First Aid (PSSM).
Accessibility and inclusion are a responsibility shared by the whole community, not just the disability service.
resources.source_pole: Source: information sheet from Efrei's disability office.
resources.national_intro: These organisations and associations are independent from the school. They can inform, support or defend your rights.
resources.assoc_intro: Chosen for the most common situations at school and for young people in education or job hunting.
resources.assoc_more: More associations: the ONISEP directory (in French)
resources.law_intro: A few simple landmarks from national texts. This is general information, not legal advice: each school or employer applies them through its own procedures, and you should always check the up-to-date texts.

def.title: Disability in law
def.text: The law of 11 February 2005 defines disability as any limitation of activity or restriction of participation in society caused by a lasting impairment of physical, sensory, mental, cognitive or psychological functions, by multiple disabilities or by a disabling health condition. It creates the right to compensation.
def.ref: Law no. 2005-102 of 11 February 2005; Code de l'action sociale et des familles, article L114

exams.title: Exam accommodations in higher education
exams.text: National texts provide exam accommodations for students with disabilities or a disabling health condition: extra time (up to one third of the total time), breaks, human or technical help, adapted papers, an adapted room. A doctor appointed by the CDAPH gives an opinion, then the institution decides and notifies its decision. Accommodations last for the whole programme leading to the degree. The disability office explains how to proceed at school.
exams.ref: Code de l'éducation, articles L112-4, D112-1 and D613-26 to D613-27-1; circular of 6 February 2023 (NOR ESRS2234137C)

rqth.title: The RQTH
rqth.text: Recognition as a disabled worker concerns anyone whose chances of getting or keeping a job are effectively reduced. The application goes to the MDPH; the CDAPH decides. It is granted for 1 to 10 years, or without time limit for a permanent impairment.
rqth.ref: Code du travail, articles L5213-1 and following

work.title: Accommodations at work
work.text: Employers take, according to needs, the appropriate measures to enable a disabled worker to get a job, do it and progress, unless they impose a disproportionate burden. Workstation or working-time adjustments are decided with the occupational physician.

quota.title: Employment obligation and funding
quota.text: Companies and public bodies with at least 20 employees must employ at least 6% of disabled workers. Financial aid exists: Agefiph for the private sector, FIPHFP for the civil service.

freedom.title: Freedom to talk about it or not
freedom.text: Employees stay free to mention their RQTH or not, at hiring or during employment. The occupational physician is bound by medical confidentiality. Rejecting a candidate because of disability or health is discrimination.
freedom.ref: Code du travail, articles L1132-1 and L5213-1

data.title: Your health data
data.text: Health and disability data are sensitive data protected by the GDPR: processing them is in principle prohibited, except in cases such as consent. HandiDiag keeps none of your answers.
